Subject: Q3 OKRs — launch plan, alignment notes, and executive approval

Team —

Attaching the first draft of the Q3 OKRs and the proposed launch plan. This is the consolidated version after leadership and product scoping sessions last week. Key asks: please review and reply with any changes by EOD Tuesday so we can lock for exec sign-off mid-week.

Top-level changes included in this draft:
- Product: two platform reliability objectives (99.95% SLO & latency P95 targets)
- Growth: move from vanity leads to ARR-qualified leads; new definition attached
- Sales: include new enterprise play metrics (see sheet tab: Sales Impact)
- Ops: retention and cost per inference targets tightened after infra review

Files attached: Q3_OKR_Draft_v1.xlsx (workbook with team-level targets).

Please focus feedback on: whether targets are realistic, any dependencies missing, and any blockers for execution. I'll collect comments and convene a 30-minute alignment huddle on Wednesday 11:00–11:30 PT if that works for leadership.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Q3 OKRs — launch plan, alignment notes, and executive approval

Marissa —

Thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes after skimming the workbook:

- Product reliability objective: move the 99.95% SLO from Engineering pillar to Platform pillar to make ownership clearer.
- Growth metric definition: suggest adding a short appendix that defines "ARR-qualified lead" and lists disqualified use cases. Keeps sales and marketing aligned.
- Ops retention stretch target: OK to keep as stretch, but add a mitigation step if retention falls below threshold in month 2.

I can take the appendix and the mitigation steps — will push a suggested update into the sheet by Monday EOD. The 11:00 Wednesday slot works for me.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Growth & GTM
Redwood Inference

Adding a sales lens here. I updated the Sales tab with a sensitivity model (attached) that shows how a 10/25/50 day ramp affects ARR by quarter — the current customer acquisition assumptions are optimistic given current funnel velocity. Suggested edits:

- Revise enterprise closed-won target down 10% as a baseline; keep the stretch at the proposed number.
- Add a metric for sales-assisted POC conversion rate (we don't track this as cleanly today).
- Recommend a cross-functional dependency: Solutions Engineering to commit to two extra POC slots per week for Q3 ramp.

Attachment: Sales_Impact_Model.pdf

Happy to walk through numbers in the alignment huddle.

--Aditya

Team —

Great work pulling the deck together. A few executive-level edits before I can sign off:

1) Consolidate the platform reliability KPI into one measurable metric (prefer SLO uptime % over a composite index).
2) Remove the top-line revenue assumption from the public-facing OKR doc (we'll keep that in the closed deck for the board).
3) Add a single slide that lists the three highest risks and mitigations for the quarter.

I asked Benedict from the board to scan the high-level targets (cc'd). He flagged that investor comms should not leak pre-approval — keep the public-facing copy gated behind the internal doc.

If no major objections, I'm ok to sign off on Thursday morning. Please confirm edits completed and leave a comment in the confluence page. I'll complete the sign-off via the DocuSign link once edits land.

Evelyn Hart
Chief Operating Officer
